transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-10
Time: 15:00 - 15:58 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Laura Gupta (Head of Platform, Pinemont), Mark Rios (Security Engineer), Diane Holloway (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick security intake to map out compliance requirements and deployment model choices. Action items captured for artifacts and benchmark plan.

---Transcript---
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh curious if we can do quick intros then jump into security scope?
[00:12] Laura Gupta: yeah hi Laura here, Head of Platform at Pinemont. we're evaluating an LLM inference layer for our private client workflows, main ask is: can we keep data in our VPC and meet SOC2 requirements.
[00:23] Mark Rios: Mark, security, also interested in audit logs and KMS, and how redwood — sorry Redwook — integrates with our HSM.
[00:31] Ethan Chen: Ethan from Redwood, SE; I'll run through the technical options and tradeoffs. quick note — we usually see three common patterns: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem).
[00:44] Diane Holloway: Diane, procurement, i'll be on the legal side, timeline is quarter end so we need clear SLOs and evidence for audits.

[00:55] Sofia: great. can we surface the SOC2/ISO needs first? Laura, what's in-scope at Pinemont for this?
[01:03] Laura: we have SOC2 Type II, userid access control, ok we only audit service providers that have clear role-based access. we need proof of encryption, KMS, and that retention is configurable. also: no customer PII should be stored outside our tenancy.
[01:20] Ethan: understood. on Redwood Hosted, we have multi-tenant hosted endpoints — SOC2 attestation covers the platform, but customers often prefer Dedicated or Private for stronger isolation and contractual data residency. we support BYOK via KMS integrations for Dedicated/Private.
[01:36] Mark: can you clarify BYOK? do you actually support external HSM and key import? or is it cloud-KMS only?
[01:43] Ethan: we support cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and have an integration path for customer-managed keys. for on-prem HSMs we typically use an envelope encryption model where the HSM wraps the data key — there is a connector pattern. i'll send the HSM playbook, it's in our security pack.
[01:58] Laura: okay, and audit logs — how long do you keep them by default? we need 1 year retained and exportable for our SIEM.
[02:08] Sofia: default retention in hosted is 90 days, Dedicated can be extended via add-on, and Private you control retention in your VPC. logs are exportable in JSONL and can be streamed to S3 or syslog.
[02:21] Mark: JSONL, good. do logs include full prompt text? that is a blocker because we don't want PII in logs.
[02:29] Ethan: there's an option to redact sensitive fields before logging. we have a log-filtering pipeline and token masking for sensitive markers. for Hosted we can enable prompt redaction rules; for Dedicated we provide config that runs pre-logger hooks in your environment.
[02:44] Laura: that sounds promising. also SSO — we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. we need RBAC mapping to our groups.
[02:54] Sofia: SSO is supported: SAML and OIDC. SCIM provisioning for user and group sync. RBAC in Console supports mapping groups to roles — e.g., viewer, admin, operator.
[03:06] Mark: does RBAC audit who invoked model rollouts or API key rotations? we need an audit trail with user IDs.
[03:13] Ethan: yes, all console actions and key operations are recorded. each action has actor, timestamp, and ip. for Hosted we store that metadata; Dedicated/Private you can also ship logs to your SIEM.
[03:27] Diane: procurement question — for Dedicated, what contract term and SLA? and is data deletion certified at termination?
[03:35] Sofia: Dedicated is typically monthly/annual reserved capacity. SLA is negotiable for enterprise; we have data deletion commitments documented in our DPA and we can provide certificate of deletion upon contract termination. we'll attach the DPA and the retention/deletion flow.
[03:51] Laura: good. are there any third-party pen tests or external audits we can share?
[03:56] Sofia: yes, SOC2 Type II report and periodic pen test summaries; we'll send redacted reports. also we have ISO in progress for certain customers — i'll include the current scope.
[04:07] Mark: question on network architecture: for Private VPC, what's the control plane connectivity? we want the control plane out-of-band, but data path must be customer routed.
[04:17] Ethan: control plane remains managed but you can choose a private control plane option. data plane in Private is deployed into your VPC, so payloads never traverse public internet. for Dedicated we offer VPC peering or PrivateLink. there are tradeoffs on management.
[04:33] Laura: ok and how about model artifacts — do you store cached KV or model weights that could include customer data?
[04:42] Ethan: runtime keeps KV cache in memory by default; we do persistent caches only in Dedicated when configured for eviction/restore. model weights are read-only artifacts and are not customer data. KV cache can be configured to not persist to disk, and in Private it's under your control.
[04:58] Mark: latency vs cost: where does Dedicated sit? we need low 50-80ms 1p95 for our workflows.
[05:06] Ethan: Dedicated can hit those SLOs depending on GPU type and batch config. Hosted is optimized for general workloads; Dedicated with pinned nodes reduces queuing and predictable latency but at higher cost. we'll propose a sizing.
[05:20] Laura: any encryption in-transit and at-rest specifics? we need TLS 1.2+, and at-rest AES-256 with KMS-based key management.
[05:29] Sofia: yes, we enforce TLS 1.2+, TLS 1.3 preferred. At-rest is AES-256, and KMS integration for envelope keys. For Hosted we manage the keys unless BYOK is enabled.
[05:40] Mark: about compliance evidence — can we get a SOC2 bridge letter during procurement?
[05:46] Sofia: yes we can provide bridge letters and redacted SOC2 report. will attach to the follow-up.
[05:51] Diane: timeline again — legal needs evidence in two weeks to start contract review.
[05:56] Sofia: note taken. we'll target artifact send by Friday.
[06:00] [longer discussion on deployment flow and handoffs — approx 10 minutes omitted for brevity]
[16:30] Ethan: (technical) one more note on keys: for AWS KMS we use GenerateDataKey and envelope encrypt, keys never leave KMS. for on-prem HSM we'll coordinate with your crypto team, there's typically a connector and we do a key wrap.
[16:48] Mark: can you share the connector docs?
[16:51] Ethan: yes, I'll include the HSM connector doc and a sample terraform snippet.
[16:55] Laura: how do we handle data retention deletion for model outputs generated during inference — like chat transcripts?
[17:03] Sofia: you can configure transcript retention per-tenant. Hosted default short, Dedicated extended via config, Private full control. also we offer a wipe API to purge specific records.
[17:15] Mark: is there a legal certification for deletion? we need a signed attestation after purge.
[17:20] Sofia: we can provide deletion receipts and S3 object deletion logs for your records.
[17:26] Laura: what's the path for a PoC — do we do a week of dedicated nodes?
[17:33] Ethan: we typically run a 1-week dedicated trial: seed with representative traffic, run latency/throughput matrix, measure token cost, KV cache hit rates. we'll need your sample prompts and traffic profile.
[17:45] Diane: budget question — is PoC billed?
[17:48] Sofia: small fee for dedicated infra for PoC, or it can be credit-backed depending on deal.
[17:54] Mark: competitors — we looked at Anthropic and some GCP endpoint options; main difference is orchestration and observability.
[18:02] Ethan: totally. we emphasize per-route tracing, token-level cost breakdown, and rollouts with automatic fallback to cheaper variants.
[18:12] Laura: can you demo the audit log export and RBAC mapping in the console?
[18:16] Sofia: we can schedule a demo. for today we'll focus on artifacts and the benchmark plan.
[18:23] [short side conversation — internet glitch causes quick drop then rejoin]
[18:58] Sofia: recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, DPA, HSM connector docs, and a benchmark plan. Pinemont will send retention policies and sample traffic.
[19:11] Laura: thanks. Mark will compile the retention/PII rules and Diane will follow-up on procurement timing.
[19:20] Sofia: perfect. any final questions?
[19:24] Mark: one micro ask — can logs include request/response hashed pointer instead of full prompt? we want traceability but not full payload.
[19:32] Ethan: yes that's supported; we can use hashed IDs and a linkable vault for full payload under very restricted access.
[19:40] Diane: that's workable.
[19:44] Sofia: ok we'll wrap. thanks all.
[19:48] End of meeting.

---Questions (captured)---
- Does Redwood support BYOK with on-prem HSM? (Answer: envelope model + connector)
- Can logs be redacted and still exportable to SIEM? (Answer: yes, with pre-logger hooks or redaction rules)
- What evidence is available for SOC2/ISO? (Answer: redacted reports, bridge letter, pen test summaries)
